ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: 4–5-day flare of very itchy, sore, red, dry rash; no specific trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Rapid worsening over the past few days; previously controlled chronic eczema.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor, dyspnea, or facial/lip/tongue swelling. No ear or neck complaints.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: Long-standing eczema treated with daily emollients (Diprobase cream, Dermol wash) and OTC hydrocortisone 1 % cream; previously trialed OTC cetirizine without benefit. No prior emergency or hospital care for skin or airway issues.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergies: “None.”
  • Medications: Diprobase cream (topical, dose/route/frequency not documented), Dermol wash (topical, frequency not documented), OTC hydrocortisone 1 % cream (topical PRN), salbutamol blue inhaler PRN (dose/frequency not documented).  
- Social context: Lives alone in London; no accompaniment noted.

Objective:
- Observable findings (video): Diffuse erythematous, dry patches on chest, hands, arms; worst in antecubital fossae. Skin cracking present; no weeping/exudate, lichenification, or scratch marks noted.
- Airway/breathing: Breathing reported as normal; no audible stridor.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert; no systemic symptoms (fever, joint pain).
- Vitals and full physical examination: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with patient: Not stated.

Assessment:
- Working impression: Worsening atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare.
  Evidence: Known history of eczema, classical flexural involvement, intense pruritus, lack of systemic infection signs, no new medications/triggers reported.
- DDx reference (consistent with transcript):
  1. Atopic dermatitis flare – most likely given chronic history and presentation.
  2. Allergic/irritant contact dermatitis – possible; acute worsening could reflect unseen exposure though patient reports no product changes.
  3. Scabies – low likelihood; pruritus overlaps but no burrows, nocturnal predominance, or household spread reported.
  (No conflicting data between transcript and DDx.)

Plan:
- Medications prescribed:
  • Fexofenadine (oral antihistamine) – dosing per prescription sent to Boots pharmacy.
  • Betnovate (topical potent corticosteroid) – apply thin layer twice daily to affected areas for 2 weeks.
- Continue current emollient regimen: Diprobase cream and Dermol wash as usual.
- Monitoring/education:
  • If no improvement or any adverse/allergic reaction to new medications, contact service sooner than 2 weeks.
  • Escalation/red-flags: development of throat swelling, breathing difficulty, widespread weeping skin, fever, or worsening rash.
- Follow-up: Routine review in 2 weeks via same service unless earlier concerns arise.
- Preventive advice: Maintain regular moisturization; avoid known irritants; consider reviewing asthma control if skin or respiratory symptoms worsen (given comorbid asthma).

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: objective vitals, full drug doses/routes/frequencies, comprehensive allergy list (foods, environmental), documentation of secondary infection signs, ENT airway screening details, auto-injector education (if risk deemed significant).  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor repetitions but clinically adequate.
